eras.name: Front-Engine Era
eras.text: Front-mounted engines dominated the opening championship years. Fangio, Farina and Ascari helped define the period; the championship used Formula 2 rules in 1952–1953 outside Indianapolis.

eras.name: Mid-Engine Revolution
eras.text: Cooper’s championship success accelerated the shift to engines behind the driver. Lighter chassis and evolving engine rules reshaped the cars; the Cosworth DFV debuted in 1967.

eras.name: Early Aero & Wing Era
eras.text: Wings became central to performance, followed by restrictions on high-mounted designs. Downforce, slick tyres and the widely used Cosworth DFV shaped this period.

eras.name: Ground Effect & Early Turbo Era
eras.text: Lotus pioneered underbody ground effect and Renault introduced turbocharging in 1977. Flat-bottom rules curtailed the first ground-effect designs from 1983, while turbo engines grew dominant before their 1989 ban.

eras.name: Electronic & Driver Aids Era
eras.text: Naturally aspirated engines returned. Active suspension, traction control and semi-automatic gearboxes advanced rapidly; most driver aids were banned for 1994, and safety changes accelerated after Imola that year.

eras.name: Aerodynamic Excess & V10 Era
eras.text: Narrower cars and grooved tyres arrived in 1998. Teams refined increasingly elaborate aerodynamic surfaces during the V10 years, with changing tyre and engine-life rules.

eras.name: Standardized V8 Era
eras.text: The 2.4-litre V8 formula replaced V10s in 2006. This period also brought KERS in 2009, a major aero reset and the introduction of DRS in 2011.

eras.name: V6 Turbo-Hybrid Era
eras.text: 1.6-litre turbocharged V6 power units combined combustion with electrical recovery through MGU-K and MGU-H systems. Energy efficiency and deployment became central to performance.

eras.text: A new aerodynamic formula used underfloor Venturi tunnels to generate much of the car’s downforce, with the aim of reducing the disturbance experienced by following cars.

eras.name: Active Aero & New Hybrid Era
eras.text: A new generation pairs active front and rear wings with revised hybrid power units, greater electrical contribution and the removal of the MGU-H. The embedded 2026 season is partial.
